def process(load_sunspots) -> pd.DataFrame:
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    import numpy as np

    df = load_sunspots.rename(columns={0: 'year', 1: 'sunspots'})
    df['year'] = df['year'].apply(lambda x: int(x))  # e.g. 1700.5 -> 1700

    # Filter 1960–2020
    mask = (df['year'] >= 1960) & (df['year'] <= 2020)
    df_sub = df[mask].reset_index(drop=True)

    values = df_sub['sunspots'].values
    years = df_sub['year'].values

    # Find maxima: prominence=20, distance=5
    max_idx, max_props = find_peaks(values, prominence=20, distance=5)
    max_years = sorted(years[max_idx])

    # Find minima: invert signal, prominence=20, distance=5
    min_idx, min_props = find_peaks(-values, prominence=20, distance=5)
    min_years = sorted(years[min_idx])

    # Estimate period using all historical data (full dataset)
    all_values = df['sunspots'].values
    all_years = df['year'].values
    all_max_idx, _ = find_peaks(all_values, prominence=20, distance=5)
    all_max_years = all_years[all_max_idx]
    # Period = average gap between consecutive maxima
    gaps = np.diff(all_max_years)
    avg_period = np.mean(gaps)

    # Top 5 maxima and minima (chronological order already, but pick top 5 by prominence)
    # Use prominence to rank, then sort top-5 by year
    max_prominence = max_props['prominences']
    top5_max_idx = max_idx[np.argsort(max_prominence)[::-1][:5]]
    top5_max_years = sorted(years[top5_max_idx])

    min_prominence = min_props['prominences']
    top5_min_idx = min_idx[np.argsort(min_prominence)[::-1][:5]]
    top5_min_years = sorted(years[top5_min_idx])

    results = pd.DataFrame({
        'avg_period': [round(avg_period, 2)],
        'top5_maxima': [top5_max_years],
        'top5_minima': [top5_min_years],
        'all_maxima_in_range': [max_years],
        'all_minima_in_range': [min_years],
        'num_maxima': [len(max_years)],
        'num_minima': [len(min_years)],
    })
    return results
input.summary: Analyze solar cycles: find peaks (maxima) and troughs (minima) in sunspot data between 1960-2020 using scipy.signal.find_peaks with prominence=20 and distance=5. Compute average period from full historical data maxima gaps. Return top 5 maxima and minima by prominence, listed in chronological order.

def process(load_sunspots) -> pd.DataFrame:
    from scipy.signal import find_peaks
    import numpy as np

    df = load_sunspots[[0, 1]].copy()
    df.columns = ['year_f', 'sunspots']
    df['year'] = df['year_f'].apply(lambda x: int(x))

    # Compute average period from ALL historical data maxima
    peaks_all, props_all = find_peaks(df['sunspots'].values, prominence=20, distance=5)
    all_peak_years = df['year'].iloc[peaks_all].values
    avg_period = round(np.mean(np.diff(all_peak_years)), 2)

    # Filter 1960–2020
    mask = (df['year'] >= 1960) & (df['year'] <= 2020)
    df_sub = df[mask].reset_index(drop=True)
    sn = df_sub['sunspots'].values
    years = df_sub['year'].values

    # Find maxima
    max_idx, max_props = find_peaks(sn, prominence=20, distance=5)
    max_years = years[max_idx].tolist()
    max_proms = max_props['prominences'].tolist()

    # Find minima (invert signal)
    min_idx, min_props = find_peaks(-sn, prominence=20, distance=5)
    min_years = years[min_idx].tolist()
    min_proms = min_props['prominences'].tolist()

    # Top 5 by prominence, then sorted chronologically
    max_top5_idx = np.argsort(max_proms)[::-1][:5]

    top5_min_years = sorted([min_years[i] for i in min_top5_idx])

    return pd.DataFrame({
        'avg_period': [avg_period],
        'top5_maxima': [top5_max_years],
        'top5_minima': [top5_min_years],
        'all_maxima_in_range': [max_years],
        'all_minima_in_range': [min_years],
        'num_maxima': [len(max_years)],
        'num_minima': [len(min_years)],
    })

Uses iloc to access first two columns (year x.5 format, yearly mean sunspots). Computes average period from full historical maxima gaps. Returns top 5 maxima and minima by prominence in chronological order.
